source: IPCC 2006 GL Vol 3 Ch 2 s2.2.1.2: 'If cement production cannot be disaggregated by type and it is suspected that significant amounts of blended and/or masonry cements are being produced in addition to portland cement, it is acceptable within good practice to assume an overall clinker fraction of 75 percent'
note: THE DOMINANT ASSUMPTION IN THIS SECTOR, and the reason the runner publishes a sensitivity rather than a single number. The activity datum is CEMENT; the emission happens when CLINKER is made, and the ratio between them is not reported by any Pakistani source. IPCC's alternative is 0.95 for essentially-all-portland production, and Pakistani mills do produce a large share of ordinary portland cement, so 0.75 is likely conservative. The 13 percent uncertainty spans 0.75 to 0.95; the runner reports both ends explicitly because a reader should see the span, not just the band.

source: IPCC 2006 GL Vol 3 Ch 2 s2.2.1.2, the alternative default where production is known to be essentially all portland cement
note: Used only for the published sensitivity. Not the central value, because Pakistani mills also produce blended and composite cements and no source disaggregates them.

note: The Tier-1 CENTRAL factor. note: The gas-balance pathway's converter: fertilizer-sector gas divided by this gives the ammonia tonnage the gas could support. The average describes modern European plants; Pakistan's older trains likely sit above it, which would LOWER the supportable tonnage and sharpen, not soften, the reconciliation's red flag.

source: IPCC 2006 GL Vol 3 Ch 3 s3.2.2.2 fallback where actual plant output is unavailable; range 0.70-0.90
note: Applied only to DOCUMENTED nameplate capacity (data/activity/ippu/facilities.csv), never to capacity inferred from production. NFDC Table 1 reports urea plants at 102 percent of installed capacity in FY2024-25, so the IPCC band is likely conservative for Pakistan; the reconciliation carries the 0.70-0.90 span rather than a point.

source: IPCC 2006 GL Vol 3 Ch 3 Eq 3.10: CO2 recovered into urea is production times 44/60; DOCUMENTATION since rc42 - the arithmetic reads pkinv.sectors.ippu.ammonia_reconciliation.UREA_CO2_RECOVERY (44/60 exactly)
note: The recovery term is the one leg of the ammonia ledger urea production determines DIRECTLY - no plant data needed. The recovered carbon is released at application, which this inventory reports under 3.H; subtracting it here is what keeps the two categories from double-counting.

A FLOOR on national ammonia when applied to urea alone: additional ammonia goes to CAN, NP, DAP and nitric acid. The product-stoichiometry pathway sums all ammoniacal products; this factor alone must never be presented as national ammonia production.

TRANSFERRED, not measured - no Pakistani stack measurement is held - and the high-pressure default beside it bounds the bracket, the kiln-intensity pattern.

source: IPCC 2006 GL Vol 3 Ch 3 Table 3.3, high-pressure plants

The screening prices that route and says the route evidence, not the factor, is what a request must confirm.
